acceptance.criterion_verbatim: BOTH halves true on the post-deploy DEPLOYED bytes and graded as one: the PUBLIC read reaches a two-slot accept path (verifyWithSlots present and reachable from verifyAccessToken and verifyRefreshToken), AND the PRIVATE read still selects ONE CURRENT key. Either half alone is a FAIL -- a two-slot private read is the defect S10E correctly barred, and a single-key public read is the defect this face exists to fix.
acceptance.invocation: Code.Location downloaded, unzipped, and searched on LITERAL markers plus an enumeration of every '.previous' occurrence with context; call sites of the minified verifyWithSlots located to establish reachability.
acceptance.output_evidence: HALF A -- THE PUBLIC READ REACHES A TWO-SLOT ACCEPT PATH, REACHABLE FROM BOTH VERIFY FUNCTIONS. verifyWithSlots is present as E8: function E8(q,$,Z,Q){ try{ return q.verify($,Z.current,Q) } catch(z){ if(!Z.previous||z.name==="TokenExpiredError") throw z; try{ return q.verify($,Z.previous,Q) } catch(J){ throw z } } }. Its call sites: async function A6(q){ let $=await lZ(); return E8(cq.default,q,$,{algorithms:["RS256"],issuer:pZ,audience:cZ}) } and async function nZ(q){ let $=await lZ(), Z=E8(cq.default,q,$,{algorithms:["RS256"]}); if(Z.type!=="refresh") throw Error("Invalid token type"); return Z }. A6 is verifyAccessToken (it carries issuer and audience) and nZ is verifyRefreshToken (it carries the type guard); BOTH take slots from lZ and BOTH call E8, so reachability is shown by the call sites rather than asserted. HALF B -- THE PRIVATE READ STILL SELECTS ONE CURRENT KEY: async function k8(){ return await mZ(B3) } with B3="opal/auth/jwt-private-key", resolving into getCurrentKey which destructures {current:J} and returns a string; and the signing site async function iZ(q){ let $=await k8(); ... sign(Z,$,{algorithm:"RS256",...}) } takes its key from k8. So SIGNING resolves through one CURRENT key and VERIFYING through two slots -- the pairing, whose half-application created this face. *** A CORRECTION ON MY OWN INSTRUMENT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY PRODUCED A FALSE FAIL: *** the first probe searched the bundle with a regex built on an ASSUMED minified shape and reported 'verifyWithSlots in the bundle: False', which taken at face value would have said this deploy failed. The regex was wrong, not the artifact. Re-run against LITERAL markers -- parseKeySlots's messages each once, TokenExpiredError 3 times, and all 7 '.previous' occurrences enumerated with context (1-3 in parseKeySlots's return shape, 4-5 in E8 itself, 6-7 in the ORIGIN secret's pre-existing overlap) -- the picture is unambiguous. A MATCHER BUILT AGAINST A FORMAT ONE HAS NOT READ RETURNS A CLEAN ZERO, and on a minified bundle the format is never the one in your head.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: The two-slot accept path REACHED on a real verify, evidenced rather than reasoned about. The genuine two-KEY test needs a previous key that does not exist until the rotation -- if so, file that limb UNCOMPUTABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION naming the rotation as where it is obtainable, and do NOT record it as passed.
acceptance.invocation: curl POST https://opalinvest.dev/auth/refresh with the token in the refresh_token COOKIE (bogus JWT, and a non-JWT value), against a no-cookie control; then .tools/aws logs filter-log-events on the function's log group over the probe window.
acceptance.output_evidence: LIMB 1, THE PATH REACHED -- EVIDENCED. Three arms with a working discriminator: no cookie returns {"error":"No refresh token"} (the guard, path NOT reached); refresh_token=<bogus JWT> and refresh_token=not-a-jwt both return {"error":"Internal server error"} (path REACHED). The two reached arms DIFFER from the guard arm, which is what makes 'reached' a measurement rather than a reading. THE LOG SAYS WHAT HAPPENED INSIDE: 'ERROR Error: W6 [JsonWebTokenError]: invalid signature' for the bogus JWT and '... jwt malformed' for the non-JWT. The first is verifyWithSlots trying current, failing, finding previous null, and RETHROWING the current-key error -- the designed behaviour of the accept path, observed on a real verify. LIMB 2, THE GENUINE TWO-KEY TEST -- UNCOMPUTABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION AND NOT RECORDED AS PASSED. It requires a token signed by the PREVIOUS key to be accepted while a CURRENT-key token is also accepted. There is no previous key: the public secret is still a BARE PEM, measured at 450 bytes with one BEGIN block and not starting with '{', so parseKeySlots returns previous=null and the fallback branch is unreachable by construction. IT IS OBTAINABLE AT THE ROTATION (TO-OP-S-10), which is the act that writes the {current, previous} envelope, and that is where this limb belongs. A NOTE THAT MATTERS FOR THE ROTATION'S SAFETY: while previous is null the new path is OBSERVABLY IDENTICAL to the old one -- before, jwt.verify threw JsonWebTokenError directly; now verifyWithSlots catches it, sees previous is null, and rethrows THE SAME ERROR OBJECT. So this deploy changes no behaviour until the envelope exists, which is the safest possible shape to land ahead of a rotation.
acceptance.denominator: 3 probe arms (1 control + 2 reached); 2 of 2 log lines attributed; 1 limb evidenced, 1 limb filed UNCOMPUTABLE with the place it becomes obtainable named.
acceptance.status_reason: SCOPE STATED EXACTLY. The criterion's primary ask -- the two-slot accept path REACHED on a real verify -- is evidenced on the wire and in the function's own log. The two-KEY limb is filed UNCOMPUTABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION and is expressly NOT recorded as passed, per the face's own instruction; it becomes obtainable only when TO-OP-S-10 writes the previous slot. PASS applies to what was asked and obtained, never to the limb that was not.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: LOGIN AND REFRESH BOTH STILL WORK after the deploy, with the invocation count stated so silence from a dead function cannot pass as health. Exercise /auth/refresh explicitly -- it is the surface this face is about and an unexercised fix on it is not evidence.

acceptance.output_evidence: REFRESH EXERCISED -- AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED TO REACH THE PATH, which is why the discriminator was needed. The first probe put the token in the JSON BODY and got {"error":"No refresh token"}, byte-identical to the no-token answer; two arms returning the same string is not evidence, and reading it as 'exercised' would have been a false pass. Cause read at source: index.ts:88 extractRefreshToken pulls the token from a COOKIE named refresh_token, never from the body. Re-probed through the cookie, the reached arms differ from the guard arm (see S10F-AC3). LOGIN STILL WORKS, exercising the SIGNING path this face must NOT have changed: a real committed credential returns 200 with mfaRequired true and a challengeId, which can only be produced by running sealCode -> getMfaCodeSealKey -> getJwtPrivateKey. THE 500 ON A BAD TOKEN IS PRE-EXISTING ROUTE BEHAVIOUR AND NOT A REGRESSION, checked rather than assumed: index.ts:233-241 handles POST /auth/refresh with no specific catch around await refresh(refreshToken), so ANY verify throw has always surfaced through the outer handler as a 500, and index.ts was not touched by this face. THE COUNTS: 32 log events over a complete window (nextToken ABSENT), 7 Invocations, 0 on the CloudWatch Errors metric, and 1 INIT_START -- a cold start on the new bundle, where a MODULE_NOT_FOUND on the changed import would have fired. NOTE THE DISCRIMINATOR ON THAT ZERO: Errors reads 0 even though two probes received a 500, because the outer handler RETURNS a 500 payload rather than failing the invocation. A handled 500 and a Lambda failure are different objects and the metric separates them -- quoting the zero without that distinction would have been the misleading half of a true number.
acceptance.denominator: 3 refresh arms + 1 login arm; 32 log events (complete window); 7 invocations; 0 Errors; 1 cold start.
acceptance.status_reason: Both surfaces exercised rather than merely unbroken, with the refresh path reached through the cookie the route actually reads, and the 500 attributed to pre-existing route handling rather than reported as a new error class.

mutant.description: The claim this face stands on is a PAIRED one: the public read now reaches a two-slot accept path AND the private read still selects one CURRENT key. The reading that would make that true on the surface and false in substance is the one this whole chain has now produced twice -- applying a single rule to a component that has two roles. A mutant that widened the PRIVATE read to two slots would satisfy 'the signer uses the shared module' and still be the defect S10E correctly barred, because it would let the signer sign under a retired key.
mutant.expected: With the private read widened to getJwtKeySlots, S10F-AC2's half B must FAIL -- the private getter would no longer resolve to a single CURRENT string -- while half A continued to pass. A criterion that graded the two halves SEPARATELY would report a partial success and let the defect through, which is precisely why the face grades them as one.
mutant.observed: Not run as a code mutation, and that is stated rather than implied: the paired criterion is graded on the DEPLOYED artifact, and planting a mutant would have required deploying a knowingly defective signer to the live login path to observe it. THE CONTROL WAS OBTAINED WITHOUT THAT, from this session's own history: the mutant already ran in production form. TO-OP-S-10E deployed exactly the single-rule-applied-to-both-roles artifact, its criterion S10E-AC2 graded PASS on accurate evidence, and the defect was found only by re-grounding -- row Z-S160. That is the mutant, its result, and the proof the paired grading is necessary rather than ceremonial. A SEPARATE INSTRUMENT CONTROL DID FIRE THIS FACE: the first bundle probe used a regex built on an assumed minified shape and reported verifyWithSlots ABSENT, which would have been a false FAIL on a correct deploy; re-run against literal markers with all 7 '.previous' occurrences enumerated, the result inverted. And the first refresh probe returned an answer byte-identical to its own control, which is what exposed that the token travels in a cookie rather than the body.

determinism.method: Load-bearing values obtained twice or on two independent instruments. (a) The artifact sha was computed by the build script, INDEPENDENTLY RECOMPUTED from the downloaded object, and PREDICTED before the apply. (b) The baseline CodeSha256 was read during the Z-S160 investigation and re-read at this face's vintage before any edit. (c) Both secrets were read at session start and after the apply. (d) Post-deploy health was read on the log text, the Invocations metric and the Errors metric. (e) The refresh path was probed on three arms including a control that must differ. (f) The bundle was searched twice -- once on assumed structure, once on literal markers -- and the disagreement resolved in favour of the literal read.
determinism.observed: STABLE where it matters, and the ONE disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed: the build sha, the independent recompute, the S3 metadata content-sha256 and the post-apply live CodeSha256 are the same value and equal the prediction; the baseline was unchanged across its two reads; both secrets identical across theirs; log text, Invocations and Errors agree once the handled-500 distinction is applied. THE DISAGREEMENT: the structural regex said verifyWithSlots was absent and the literal search said present. That is not instrument noise -- it is one broken probe and one sound one, and the sound one is corroborated by the enumerated call sites and by the live log showing the accept path executing. The broken probe is reported in full rather than discarded, because a reader who repeats it will get the same wrong answer.
